items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the civil service law, the retirement and social security law
and the criminal procedure law, in relation to transferring the regional state
park police to the division of state police; and to repeal certain provisions
of the parks, recreation and historic preservation law, relating thereto
items.lawCode: Amd §58, Civ Serv L; amd §§381-b & 363-b, R & SS L; rpld §9.05 sub 4, §13.17, Pks & Rec L; amd §1.20, CP L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4647

SPONSOR: GOUNARDES
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil service law, the retirement and social securi-
ty law and the criminal procedure law, in relation to transferring the
regional state park police to the division of state police; and to
repeal certain provisions of the parks, recreation and historic preser-
vation law, relating thereto

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To merge the State Park Police with the State Police by reclassifying
all aspects of the Regional State Park Police.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sections one through section seven of this bill are devoted to the
transfer of functions, personnel, facilities, records, vehicles, equip-
ment, unfinished business, pending actions, rules, regulations, acts,
orders, determinations, decisions and legal designations of the Office
of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation pertaining to the func-
tions and powers of the Regional State Park Police as detailed in the
Civil Service Law to the Superintendent of State Police.

Section seven provides that no action pending against the Office of
Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation at the time this act takes
effect shall be affected by this act.

Sections eight through nine of this bill provide that all remaining
appropriations (first to the State Comptroller and subsequently made
available for use by the Division of State Police), assets and liabil-
ities of the Regional State Park Police shall be transferred to and
assumed by the Division of State Police.  The Superintendent of State
Police shall be charged generally with the duty and shall be the power
to classify and reclassify all member positions in the Division of State
Police subject to the approval of the Director of the Budget.

Sections ten and eleven make conforming changes to Civil Service Law.

Section twelve through fourteen amend Retirement and Social Security Law
to add the newly transferred members to the retirement benefit
provisions currently governing the Division of State Police.

Section fifteen provides that no existing right or remedy shall be lost
or impaired by reason of this act.

Section sixteen provides that the provisions of this act shall supersede
inconsistent provisions of other law.

Section seventeen removes a reference to the regional state park police
in section 9.05 of the parks, recreation and historic preservation law.

Section eighteen repeals section 13.17 of the parks, recreation and
historic preservation law which establishes the regional state park
police.


Section nineteen removes a reference to the regional state park police
in section 1.20 of criminal procedure law.

Section twenty is a severability clause.

Section twenty-one of the bill provides that this act shall take effect
immediately.

 
EXISTING LAW:

Currently, the Regional State Park Police is a unit of the Office of
Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation and are not included as a
unit of the Division of the State Police.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill would merge the State Park Police with the State Police which
will result in cost savings for the academy and training for both forc-
es. Additionally the merger will address the high rate of attrition
faced by the State Park Police while eliminating duplication of services
and equipment. It will also reduce overtime costs incurred by the State
Park Police as a standalone unit.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: S3676A - Referred to Civil Service and Pensions

2019: S3676 - Referred to Civil Service and Pensions

2017-2018: S.5267A - Referred to Civil Service and Pensions

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

See bill.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
